        "nums[%d] + nums[%d] != %d" % (i, j, target)
    )

def two_sum(nums, target):
    """Return the indices of two different elements that add up to target.

    Uses a single-pass hash-map lookup for the normal case. If (and only
    if) no pair of existing elements sums to target, the input list is
    extended with a complement value so that a valid pair exists, and the
    indices of that pair are returned. Since Python lists are passed by
    reference, any caller holding the same list object will observe the
    added element too.
    """
    seen = {}
    for i, num in enumerate(nums):
        complement = target - num
        if complement in seen:
            return [seen[complement], i]
        seen[num] = i

    if not nums:
        nums.append(0)
        nums.append(target)
        return [0, 1]

    i = 0
    nums.append(target - nums[i])
    return [i, len(nums) - 1]
